sources.note: Step 212's evidence-driven architecture audit methodology: a five-value implementation-status classification, an evidence-quality ladder E0-E5, five gap classes G1-G5, ownerless/shared-ownership invariant checks, contract/state-machine/replay audit methods, and a 15-item provisional gap register G-01..G-15, all explicitly gated by 'no evidence => Unknown' (never Missing or Implemented).

rows.anchor: Status(I) in {Implemented, Partial, Specified, Missing, Unknown} ... Unknown != Missing ... Unknown != Implemented
rows.statement: Defines a five-value implementation-status classification for every architectural property (Implemented/Partial/Specified/Missing/Unknown), with boxed guardrails Unknown!=Missing and Unknown!=Implemented -- the distinction between Missing and Unknown is called critical.

rows.anchor: We derive a good architectural principle and gradually begin speaking about it as though the existing system already implements it. That would be architectural hallucination ... Derived Architecture != Current Architecture
rows.statement: Names the risk of 'architectural hallucination' -- gradually treating a derived architectural principle as though the existing system already implements it -- and sets a strict boundary Derived Architecture != Current Architecture, requiring the current architecture to be established from evidence.

rows.anchor: G_i=(I_i,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap)
rows.statement: Defines a per-invariant evidence record G_i=(Invariant,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap) as the unit of the architecture audit.

rows.anchor: I1 Identity ≠ State ... I15 No silent semantic strengthening ... none of these should yet be marked 'Implemented' merely because we derived them
rows.statement: Lists a first 15-item theoretical assurance register (I1-I15: Identity!=State, historical version preservation, provenance preservation, epistemic status preservation, Unknown!=False, uncertainty preservation, model-version integrity, Inference!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, contradiction preservation, temporal validity, legal state transitions, pre/postconditions, no silent semantic strengthening), explicitly marked as targets not yet verified as implemented.

rows.anchor: E_0=No evidence ... E_5=Formal verification
rows.statement: Defines a six-level evidence-quality hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E5 (formal verification), via E1 claim/documentation, E2 static implementation evidence, E3 executable test evidence, E4 runtime/production evidence, worked through a provenance example progressing from documentation claim to automated evidence-chain test to production lineage recording.

rows.anchor: Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I)
rows.statement: Separates evidence strength from confidence: strong (E2) evidence from inspecting only one module may still leave confidence in system-wide enforcement low; Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I).

rows.anchor: The architecture is 82% compliant ... unless we have first defined ... population ... weighting ... independence ... evidence quality ... confidence model ... treatment of critical properties
rows.statement: Warns against stating an unsupported compliance percentage (e.g. '82% compliant') without first defining the requirement population, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model and treatment of critical properties; recommends a qualitative CriticalGap measure instead.

rows.anchor: G1 — Semantic gap ... G5 — Assurance gap ... These gaps can coexist
rows.statement: Distinguishes five coexisting gap classes: G1 Semantic (software loses domain meaning), G2 Governance (authority/responsibility ambiguous), G3 Temporal (historical state not reconstructable), G4 Epistemic (evidence/uncertainty/assumptions lost), G5 Assurance (behavior may be correct but insufficiently evidenced).

rows.anchor: Implementation = Present but Assurance = Weak. This is not necessarily an implementation gap. It is an: Assurance Gap
rows.statement: Worked example distinguishing implementation presence from assurance: modelVersion correctly stored (Implementation=Present) but with no automated test proving it survives the workflow (Assurance=Weak) is classified specifically as an Assurance Gap, not an implementation gap.

rows.anchor: ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap
rows.statement: Distinguishes Architecture gap (design itself lacks the mechanism), Implementation gap (mechanism specified but code does not implement it correctly), and Verification gap (implementation appears correct but evidence is insufficient) as three non-identical gap types.

rows.anchor: TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing ... Ownerless Invariants ... Shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility
rows.statement: Identifies a governance gap pattern where a technical mechanism (AI->Assessment->Approval) works but nobody has defined who is authorized to approve, so TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing; introduces the 'ownerless invariant' search (Owner(I)=empty set, dangerous because nobody maintains it) and its converse, the 'shared ownership' problem, where undivided shared responsibility (Owner(I)={A,B,C}) risks each team assuming another enforces the invariant -- boxed as 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'.

rows.anchor: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) ... Loss(C)={p | p in CriticalProperties and p absent after transformation}
rows.statement: Defines a semantic-loss function for a context-to-context contract L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C), refined to Loss(C) as the set of critical properties absent after transformation; worked example: an Assessment=(score,uncertainty,modelVersion,evidenceRef) contract sending only {score} loses uncertainty/modelVersion/evidenceRef, a Critical Semantic Gap if downstream governance requires them.

rows.anchor: ΔT=T_target △ T_actual where △ denotes symmetric difference ... Unauthorized State Transition Path
rows.statement: Proposes reconstructing actual state-machine transitions T_actual from implementation and comparing to target transitions T_target via symmetric difference DeltaT = T_target triangle T_actual as a state-transition gap measure; a transition present in T_actual but absent from T_target is an Unauthorized State Transition Path warranting high priority when governance consequences exist.

rows.anchor: Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t) ... Reproducibility ... Replayability ... A system may be replayable without being perfectly reproducible
rows.statement: Defines historical replay Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t), noting exact replay (Replay(A,t)=A_t) may be impossible when external conditions change, in which case the system should preserve enough provenance to explain why; distinguishes Reproducibility (can we regenerate the same result, F(X,M)=Y again) from Replayability (can we reconstruct what happened and why), noting a system may be replayable without being reproducible (e.g. a now-defunct external service).

rows.anchor: A new state does not necessarily know the old state ... CurrentState + HistoricalProvenance ... History must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state
rows.statement: Gives a technically disciplined reading of an earlier 'Chapter 4' observation ('a new state does not necessarily know the old state'): rejects CurrentState=History, proposing instead CurrentState+HistoricalProvenance as sufficient for reconstructing relevant prior meaning; boxed principle: history must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state.

rows.anchor: Prediction -> AutomaticAuthority ... CurrentState -> AssumeCompleteHistory ... Unknown -> False ... Execution -> AssumeSuccess ... Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions
rows.statement: States a negative-space design principle: a mature architecture must specify ForbiddenPaths as well as AllowedPaths (Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions), and lists four named forbidden implicit transitions to guard against: Prediction->AutomaticAuthority, CurrentState->AssumeCompleteHistory, Unknown->False, Execution->AssumeSuccess.

lineage_claims.quote: We can extend the AAG

rows.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
rows.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

rows.anchor: G-01 Identity ... G-15 History ... This is the audit instrument
rows.statement: Defines a 15-item provisional gap register (G-01 through G-15) as concrete audit questions (identity/state separation, historical reconstructability, provenance traceability, uncertainty preservation across boundaries, model/version provenance, inference-to-authority escalation, decision/execution separation, execution/outcome separation, illegal transition blocking, contract semantic loss, contradiction coexistence, unknown-vs-false distinguishability, automatic critical-invariant testing, single accountable ownership, prior semantic context reconstruction).

rows.anchor: No evidence => Unknown. Not: No evidence => Missing. And certainly not: No evidence => Implemented
rows.statement: States the methodological rule of Step 212 as most important: the gap register's rows must not be populated by imagination but from actual KnowledgeOS artifacts, with the default for absence of evidence being No evidence=>Unknown, explicitly not =>Missing and certainly not =>Implemented.

rows.anchor: ### Architectural reasoning PASS ... Gītā Chapters 1–4 COHERENT
rows.statement: Step 212 verdict: architectural reasoning, DDD, mathematics, statistics, and AI dimensions each rated PASS; Gita chapters 1-4 rated COHERENT (continuing to generate architectural questions without being presented as technical proof).

lineage_claims.quote: The next step should not introduce another theoretical layer. It should begin the evidence audit.

rows.anchor: FACT | DERIVED | PROPOSED | UNKNOWN ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Evidence ... architectural invention [to] architectural archaeology
rows.statement: Previews Step 213 (Evidence-First Reconstruction): every architectural claim will be tagged FACT|DERIVED|PROPOSED|UNKNOWN and connected via Invariant->Implementation->Evidence; frames this as the point where the work shifts from 'architectural invention' to 'architectural archaeology', needed so the eventual book can credibly claim the theory emerged from real engineering experience rather than being designed retrospectively and projected onto the software.

rows.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
rows.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

rows.anchor: the corpus contradicts itself on the scope of the derivation phase
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation,' while Step 212 Section 212.33 scopes the reconstruction to 'the artifacts already generated during Steps 1-182 and later implementation material' -- so the corpus declares derivation runs 1-211 while reconstruction covers only 1-182, and the resulting 29-33-step gap is never reconciled anywhere in the band.

rows.anchor: The band is a five-deep chain of deferral
rows.statement: Step 215 produces a 14-code type taxonomy (glossary), a 20-column header list (text fence), a 5-row placeholder matrix (28/40 cells '...'), a 3-phase workflow, and a closing pointer to Step 216 -- i.e. FORWARD POINTER, not an artifact. Verbatim deferral chain: 212->213 ('the next stage should be an evidence-driven reconstruction'); 213->214 ('create the first Evidence Ledger'); 214->215 ('the next step should be retrospective reconstruction'); 215->216 ('Step 216 should not be another theoretical step... it should be the actual execution of the reconstruction'); 216->? ('we should not yet write another architectural theory step', out of scope). Four consecutive files each announce that the *next* file will do the empirical work; the audit announced in Step 212 has not begun by the end of Step 215.

rows.anchor: The three files that announce empirical work ... DO NOT BREAK THE PATTERN
rows.statement: Decisive verdict: Step 212 'Architecture Gap Discovery', Step 213 'Evidence-First Reconstruction' and Step 214 'Build the Evidence Ledger' each announce empirical work and each performs none -- zero shell commands, repository reads, file paths, commit hashes, test-runner output, directory listings, or tool invocations in any of the eight files. The corpus's prior 465-file/207-step record of zero empirical acts is extended, unbroken, to 215 steps and 473 files. Each of the three files states its own non-execution explicitly: Step 212 Section 212.32 ('No evidence => Unknown') then assigns no status to any row; Step 213 Section 213.3 ('each artifact is evidence') then opens no artifact; Step 214 Section 214.1 defines a 10-tuple ledger then records no ledger entry. Under TEST SPECIFIED != TEST EXECUTED, all 15 invariants I1-I15 and all 15 gaps G-01-G-15 remain at 'specified'.

rows.anchor: Step 210's matrix instantiates, in 12 of its 15 rows, the two failure modes Step 212 names two files later — and neither file notices
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 warns explicitly against 'Ownerless Invariants' (I exists but Owner(I) = empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints the same 15 invariants from Step 210 with the Owner column deleted entirely, and performs no such search -- discarding the exact data (Step 210's Owner column, with 7/15 ownerless and 5/15 shared) that would have triggered Step 212's own diagnosis.

rows.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
rows.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

rows.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). ZERO — the only file in the band that cites no prior step by number at all
rows.statement: Step 211 opens by referring to 'the Invariant Verification Matrix' by title, not number, and its Section 211.32 ('Connection to our earlier work') names six disciplines (DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, AI engineering, the Gita lens) and zero steps. Later response in scope: Step 212 Section 212.30 extends the AAG diagram with a forbidden edge (Assessment -X-> Authority); Step 213 Section 213.33 extends it to EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture).

rows.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: Status(I) 5-valued; Unknown != Missing; Unknown != Implemented; architectural hallucination; G_i 7-tuple; No evidence => Unknown
rows.statement: Step 212 ('Architecture Gap Discovery') defines Status(I) in {Implemented,Partial,Specified,Missing,Unknown} boxed with Unknown!=Missing and Unknown!=Implemented; boxes 'Derived Architecture != Current Architecture'; names 'architectural hallucination' (deriving a good principle and gradually speaking as though the system already implements it); defines a gap record G_i=(I_i,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap); an E_0..E_5 evidence-quality scale; Confidence(I)!=EvidenceLevel(I); Gap(I)=Target(I)-Current(I) with Gap(I) in {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}; five gap classes G1(semantic)-G5(assurance); boxes ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap; boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' and 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'; L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C); Loss(C) as a set of absent critical properties; DeltaT=T_target symmetric-difference T_actual; Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t); and boxes 'No evidence => Unknown' plus a G-01..G-15 gap-question register and an I1-I15 target register.

rows.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). ZERO individual steps — only two ranges (Steps 1-211, Steps 1-182)
rows.statement: Step 212 cites no individual prior step by number, only two ranges (Steps 1-211 in Section 212.5, Steps 1-182 in Section 212.33). Later response in scope: Step 213 adopts the epistemic discipline and recasts it as F/D/P/U; Step 215 Section 215.30's prohibition on 'assume implementation' echoes Step 212 Section 212.32.

rows.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES/UNRESOLVED — 'the step titled Gap Discovery discovers zero gaps'; DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the discipline, INCOMPLETE on the instrument
rows.statement: Step 212's five-valued status with the two boxed non-inferences (Unknown!=Missing, Unknown!=Implemented) and 'architectural hallucination' (Section 212.2, 'we derive a good architectural principle and gradually begin speaking about it as though the existing system already implements it') is judged the clearest and most valuable definitional work in the band, precisely naming the pathology this whole verification programme exists to catch. Against this, the G_i 7-tuple has no instance populated anywhere, and E_0..E_5 contradicts Step 210's E_1..E_5 (Contradiction #3).

rows.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 212.19's L(C) subtraction repeats Step 208's forbidden move without the caveat, four files later
rows.statement: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) (Section 212.19) re-performs Step 208 Section 208.10's subtraction on an undefined information measure, this time without Step 208's own caveat ('we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure') and without citing it -- the fourth occurrence of this defect in the band (208.3, 208.10, 212.19, 214.7). Section 212.19's own next sentence and its set-valued Loss(C) partially rescue this as a refinement, but the subtraction is stated first. Secondary, less severe: Section 212.10's Gap(I)=Target(I)-Current(I) is written as an equation then immediately declared 'a conceptual relation' since architecture properties are not always numerical -- an honest self-limit, the third instance in the band of write-the-arithmetic-then-disclaim-the-scale.

rows.anchor: COMPUTABILITY and TABLE-CELL AUDIT: 104 cells, 0 placeholders, 0 determinations — the Status column does not exist in any table
rows.statement: Status(I) is DEFINED but assigned to 0 of 15 invariants; G_i is DEFINED with 0 instances; the 15 G-01..G-15 questions are DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (well-posed) but 0 answered; DeltaT and Replay(A,t) are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (require reading code/an artifact, neither is done); Loss(C) is DEFINED but CriticalProperties is never enumerated for any C. Machine-counted table audit: the field glossary (7x2, 14 cells), the target register (15x3, 45 cells, column 3 holding 'Required' not a status), and the gap register (15x3, 45 cells, column 3 holding a question not an answer) total 104 cells, 0 placeholders, and 0 determinations -- the Status column, the entire point of the step, exists in no table. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED: four designed audits (context-boundary, contract, state-machine, historical-replay) answer their per-item questions for zero items.

rows.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: VERY STRONG on discipline (Confidence != EvidenceLevel; six preconditions for a compliance percentage), VACUOUS on data; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: mostly correct with one recurrence of the subtraction defect
rows.statement: Section 212.8's Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I) ('E_2 may be strong evidence of implementation, but if we only inspected one module, confidence in system-wide enforcement may remain low') correctly names the sampling-frame distinction. Section 212.9 lists six preconditions for any compliance percentage (population of requirements, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model, treatment of critical properties) and refuses the number without them -- judged the strongest anti-fabrication passage in the corpus. Against this, zero evidence is actually gathered, so the discipline has nothing to discipline. Measurement: Status(I) and Gap(I) classes are nominal with no arithmetic, correct, except Gap(I) in {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown} is a 'nominal-with-an-outlier' set (Unknown breaks the otherwise-ordinal sequence) which the file does not notice, making any later aggregation over Gap ill-defined; E_0..E_5 is a correctly-labelled ordinal hierarchy but recalibrated relative to Step 210 (Contradiction #3); DeltaT as set symmetric difference is correctly typed, the cleanest formal move in the file.

rows.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on method (Ownerless Invariants; ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap; the negative-space principle), decisive deficiency: it names its predecessor's flaws and then discards the data needed to apply them
rows.statement: Section 212.15 (Ownerless Invariants) and Section 212.16 (shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility) are correct DDD governance concerns; Section 212.17's five per-context questions and Section 212.21's DeltaT audit are the right instruments; Section 212.29's Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions (negative-space principle) is a real, under-appreciated point. Decisive deficiency: Sections 212.15/212.16 are exact diagnoses of Step 210's own Owner column (11 of 15 rows problematic), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints those same 15 invariants with the Owner column deleted -- discarding the evidence that would have triggered its own two findings (Contradiction #7).

rows.anchor: UL NOTES: 'Architectural hallucination' a strong coinage; 'Gap' now denotes four different things across two files; ASSUMPTIONS/UNDEFINED SYMBOLS
rows.statement: 'Architectural hallucination' (Section 212.2) is a strong, precise coinage; Missing vs Unknown is carefully distinguished. Against this, 'Gap' now denotes four different things in the band: a numeric difference (Section 212.10), an ordinal category (Section 211.4 and Section 212.10, two different category sets), a class (G1-G5, Section 212.11), and a register row (G-01-G-15, Section 212.31). Assumptions: status is single-valued per invariant; evidence can be found by inspection; T_actual is recoverable from implementation. Hidden: that someone will do the inspection (the file is written imperatively for an unnamed future actor); that the 15 target invariants are the right target (inherited unreconciled from Step 210, itself unreconciled from Step 209's 8); that Target(I) is known (the Target column says 'Required' for 13 of 15, a modality not a target level, so Current cannot be subtracted from it); that deleting the Owner column is lossless (it is not -- it discards exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 need). Undefined symbols: Target(I), Current(I), InformationBefore/After(C), CriticalProperties(C), T_actual, F in Replay(A,t)=F(...), Confidence(I) codomain, Mechanism.

rows.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 212, including the word 'Discovery' itself
rows.statement: Survives: Unknown != Missing != Implemented; Derived Architecture != Current Architecture; architectural hallucination as a named risk; the boxed 'No evidence => Unknown' as the correct default; Confidence != EvidenceLevel; the six preconditions for a compliance percentage; ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap; Ownerless Invariants; DeltaT symmetric difference; the negative-space principle; the 15 gap questions as a usable audit instrument. Does not survive: any actual gap, status, or L(C) as arithmetic; Gap(I)=Target-Current as an equation; the word 'Discovery' in the title, since the step discovers zero gaps.

rows.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
rows.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

rows.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
rows.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
rows.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
rows.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

rows.anchor: Total new identifiers minted in this band: 162
rows.statement: Inventory of new identifier families minted across Steps 208-215: I_L/I_C/I_S (3), I_KOS members (8), P_1-P_4 (4), L_1-L_2 (2), I1-I15 (15, reprinted in 212), E_1-E_5 v1 (5), A_s..A_g (6), C0-C4 (5), situations A-D (4), AuthorityLevel states (5), E_0-E_5 v2 recalibrated (6), G1-G5 (5), G-01-G-15 (15), Status(I) values (5), Gap(I) v1 (5), Gap(I) v2 different set (5), F/D/P/U (4), E_1-E_5 primary/secondary split (2), KState values (8), ELG edge types (7), 14-code type taxonomy (14), Epoch_1-Epoch_5 (5), architecture senses (4) -- totalling 162 new identifiers minted in this 8-file band, excluding one-off symbols.

rows.anchor: STEP 212 load-bearing boxed claims: Derived != Current Architecture, No evidence => Unknown (implying all 15 invariants are Unknown), Ownerless Invariants (data deleted)
rows.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 212: (1) 'Derived Architecture != Current Architecture' -- survives, the correct guard against architectural hallucination, which the file itself names. (2) 'No evidence ⇒ Unknown' (with companions Unknown!=Missing, Unknown!=Implemented) -- survives as the band's most important epistemic rule; by this rule all 15 invariants and all 15 gaps are Unknown as of Step 215. (3) 'Ownerless Invariants' -- survives as a diagnostic, but the file deletes the data (Step 210's Owner column) needed to apply it (Contradiction #7).

rows.anchor: O-5 — Four-to-five-deep deferral chain.
rows.statement: 212->213->214->215->216, each announcing that the next step does the empirical work. Step 216 (out of scope, first line inspected only) defers again.

rows.anchor: O-10 — Steps 212, 213, 214 produce no data.
rows.statement: Step 212: 104 table cells, 0 placeholders, 0 statuses assigned, 0 gaps determined -- its registers hold targets and questions, and the Status column that is the point of the step exists in no table. Step 213: 0 artifacts opened. Step 214: 0 ledger rows -- fewer than the uncited Step 109 Section 109.69, which produced 4 fabricated example rows. EL=union_i EL_i is boxed over an empty index set.

rows.anchor: O-13 — Measurement discipline is bimodal: five correct refusals, six scale violations.
rows.statement: Correct refusals: Section 209.21 (declines a universal total order on epistemic states), Section 210.29 (declines to scalarize assurance, names fake precision), Section 211.4 (declines numeric gap values), Section 212.9 (six preconditions for a percentage), Section 214.23 (declines a linear KState lifecycle, permits co-occurrence), Section 215.7 (declines to convert a count into a quality score). Violations: I(A)<I(E) and L(C)=I_req-I_pres on an explicitly undefined measure (208.3/208.10, repeated 212.19, 214.7); S(T(x))>S(x) on the order 209.21 declines (209.25, 210.9); min{Assurance(...)} on the vector 211.17 forbids scalarizing (211.6); cardinal A_s=1,A_p=0 on 211.4's ordinal dimensions (211.17); Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) on the scale 210.29 declines (210.28); the proportionality on two scaleless quantities (215.10). Scale-integrity failure: the E_n evidence ladder has two incompatible calibrations (210.30 vs 212.6) differing on E_2, E_3, E_4 -- any statement 'this has E_4 evidence' is uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under.
