sources.note: Rereads Gita Chapter 5 (Karma-sannyasa-yoga) not as an additional layer but as the chapter explaining the kernel's OPERATIONAL DISCIPLINE, inserted after the Chapters 6-18 sequence was built. Contributes: Operation execution != operation authorship (from doer-identification verses), directly feeding provenance/authority separation; a five-factor Action=f(Actor,Operation,Context,Effort,Contingency) decomposition (explicitly not five new primitives); the city-of-nine-gates analogy as a kernel BOUNDARY/interface concept; Operation validity != desired outcome (a deterministic-assurance principle: neither failure disproves valid qualification nor success proves it); a NormalizePerspective operator with explicit caution that this does not solve Step 287's semantic equality problem; a stable-Buddhi invariant d(K,x,c) approx d(K2,x,c2) under decision-irrelevant perturbations; desire/fear/anger modeled as bias/perturbation functions Buddhi must distinguish from signal; and the culminating separation Knowledge State K_t != Kernel State (fraktur K)_t, with final formula K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))).

rows.anchor: Operation execution \neq operation authorship
rows.statement: From 5.27's 'I am the doer' bewilderment (activities actually carried out through the modes of nature, not imported theologically): proposes Operation execution != operation authorship, decomposing Operation into intent, actor, mechanism, context, authorization, execution, result -- assessed as precisely the separation the existing provenance/authority model needs. Also, from 5.8-9's five causes of action (doer, work, situation, endeavor, fortune, not promoted as five primitives), proposes the analytical decomposition Action=f(Actor,Operation,Context,Effort,Contingency), reinforcing the principle 'do not collapse operation, actor, context, authority and outcome into one object'.
invariants: do not collapse operation, actor, context, authority and outcome into one object

rows.anchor: Operation validity \neq desired outcome
rows.statement: From 5.10-12 (relinquishing attachment to fruit): Operation validity != desired outcome -- 'the system must evaluate whether an operation was epistemically/technically justified independently of whether it produced the desired result'. Worked example: Hypothesis->Qualification->Action->Outcome=failure does not automatically mean Qualification=invalid; conversely Outcome=success does not prove Qualification=valid -- assessed as a profound connection to deterministic assurance.
invariants: operation validity is independent of outcome

rows.anchor: the interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary
rows.statement: From 5.13's city of nine gates (the self not identifying with the body's activities): proposes a kernel boundary concept distinguishing internal reasoning (state/Buddhi/qualification/transformation) from external interfaces (input/output, observation/action) -- 'the gates' understood as interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary, treated strictly as a philosophical model, not literal architecture.

rows.anchor: we should not claim that Chapter 5 solves semantic equality ... it does not provide the decision procedure for K_1\equiv K_2
rows.statement: From 5.18's equal vision (wise person sees equally despite differences in external form): proposes NormalizePerspective(x) -- distinguish superficial representation from underlying epistemic identity, normalizing different representations before comparing underlying semantics. Explicitly and critically caveats: the Gita provides a philosophical hypothesis for why deeper equivalence matters, but does NOT provide the decision procedure for K_1 equiv K_2 (the Step 287 equality problem remains unsolved).
missing: the actual K_1 equiv K_2 decision procedure

rows.anchor: Kernel invariant: discrimination should remain stable under perturbation ... d(K,x,c) \approx d(K',x,c')
rows.statement: From 5.20's sthira-buddhi (steady, unbewildered intelligence): proposes the kernel invariant that discrimination should remain stable under perturbation. Formalizes Buddhi(K,x,c)->d and proposes stability means d(K,x,c) approx d(K',x,c') under changes that are not decision-relevant -- explicitly connected to (but not identical with) the provenance/equality work. From 5.23/5.27-28, models desire, fear and anger (not literalized as human emotion) as biasing perturbations: constructs B(K,x) as a bias/perturbation function that Buddhi must discriminate from signal -- highly relevant to AI systems.
missing: formal definition of 'decision-relevant' changes
invariants: d(K,x,c) approx d(K',x,c') under decision-irrelevant perturbation

rows.anchor: Q(K_{t+1}) > Q(K_t) ... 100 pieces of noisy knowledge \downarrow purification \downarrow 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge
rows.statement: From 5.11 (purification through disciplined action without attachment): sharpens purification from |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| to Q(K_{t+1})>Q(K_t) where Q is a future epistemic-quality function. Concrete illustration: a kernel could transform 100 pieces of noisy knowledge into 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge, becoming better despite becoming smaller -- assessed as a major correction to a purely information-quantity model.
missing: formal definition of Q

rows.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Kernel State ... A kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode.
rows.statement: Explicit separation: Knowledge State K_t answers 'what does the system currently represent/know', Kernel State (fraktur K)_t = (K_t,M_t,B_t,Z_t,Pi_t) answers 'in what condition is the system currently processing that knowledge'. K_t != (fraktur K)_t: a kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode, or hold incomplete knowledge with excellent discrimination/qualification behaviour -- assessed as very important for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model. Candidate kernel transition: (fraktur K)_t --Buddhi--> o_t --Purify--> (fraktur K)_{t+1}. Final consolidated formula: K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))). Concluding principle: the Kernel is not the Knowledge; the Kernel is the smallest active unit that operates on Knowledge.

rows.statement: Headline correction: K is NOT the foundational layer of the theory — it is derived, three layers above the true base, which is the typed primitive triple (Entity universe, Dimension universe, dimension-indexed value spaces) from Q14; the previously suspected circularity T->K->Invariants->T is dissolved once invariants are correctly re-typed as predicates OVER K rather than components stored inside it — 'predicates over a structure are not part of the structure'.

rows.anchor: LAYER 0 PRIMITIVE ℰ (entities) 𝒟 (dimensions) V_D (value spaces) Time Origin ... LAYER 1 CONTENT P = (E,D,V) Observation ... LAYER 4 STATE 𝒜 = Set(Assertion) ℛ ⊆ 𝒜×𝒜×Type K = (𝒜,ℛ) ... LAYER 6 DYNAMICS T ... LAYER 7 DERIVED Assessment → Σ Validation Γ Invariants ... LAYER 8 RECORD History Lineage. E
rows.statement: A strict nine-layer dependency stack is derived for the whole theory: Layer 0 Primitive (Entities, Dimensions, Value spaces, Time, Origin), Layer 1 Content (Proposition, Observation), Layer 2 Qualified (Evidence, Context, Identity), Layer 3 Claim (Assertion), Layer 4 State (Assertion set, Relations, K), Layer 5 Norm (Policy, Authority), Layer 6 Dynamics (Transformation T), Layer 7 Derived (Assessment/Sigma, Validation, Gamma, Invariants), Layer 8 Record (History, Lineage) — every dependency arrow points strictly upward, with no arrow returning to a lower layer.

rows.anchor: Time PRIMITIVE ... Content (ℰ,𝒟,V_D) PRIMITIVE ... K (𝒜,ℛ) DERIVED ... Policy 5-tuple primitive at layer 5 — but see G-P1 ... Authority competence primitive — binding UNDEFINED ... Σ (dir,str) DERIVED ... Lineage Π ∘ ℛ_der* DERIVED O(n+m)
rows.statement: All nineteen theory objects (Time, Origin, Content/primitives, Observation, Evidence, Context, Provenance, Identity, Assertion, K, Policy, Authority, Invariant, Transformation, Assessment, Sigma, Gamma, Decision, History, Lineage) are tabulated with type, primitive-or-derived status, kind (metadata/state/policy/assessment/event/operation/relation), dependencies, whether a base case exists, and computability — every object has a base case, and Authority is flagged with its binding as UNDEFINED even though it is otherwise primitive.

rows.statement: Explicit architectural correction: Step 284 (Book Architecture Gate) must not be made to wait for Steps 285-289 (computational/empirical/measurement/governance/end-to-end certification), because doing so would recreate the same category error (conflating theory closure with implementation/empirical/governance completeness) that Steps 280-283 were spent eliminating; the book gate can and should operate with FC=TRUE, CC/GC at whatever their known actual status is, and EC=FALSE, as long as those statuses are stated accurately rather than silently upgraded.

rows.anchor:
# STEP 290 — FINAL CERTIFICATION DECISION

Only now should there be another global closure decision.

It should calculate independently:

$$
\mathcal C =
(FC,CC,EC,GC)
$$

and issue one of:

### A — Theory remains open ... ### B — Theory closed, certification incomplete ... ### C — Fully certified
rows.statement: Defines Step 290 (Final Certification Decision) as the only point at which another global closure decision should occur, computing the 4-tuple C=(FC,CC,EC,GC) independently and choosing among three outcomes: A (theory remains open, only if a genuine theory-critical contradiction or insufficiency is discovered), B (theory closed but certification incomplete, if FC=TRUE while implementation/empirical/governance certification remain incomplete), or C (fully certified, only if all required dimensions are actually evidenced); explicitly preserves the FC!=CC!=EC!=GC rule and forbids inferring EC or GC from FC-and-CC.

rows.statement: Composes three lenses into a pipeline: Zero ('do we have a basis?' -> NO_BASIS if not), Leonardo ('is the relevant context sufficiently represented?' -> INCOMPLETE_CONTEXT if not), Statistical Learning ('what model learns best given the context?'), then Assessment ('does it generalize?') -> Knowledge. sources.note: Step 180 distinguishes Unknown (Case A: no reliable evidence either way, E=empty) from Contradictory (Case B: E1->C and E2->not-C, evidence exists on both sides) -- Unknown != Contradictory, a genuinely new distinction beyond the prior True/False/Unknown three-valued logic. Proposes a provisional seven-state epistemic space E = {Unasserted,Candidate,Supported,Established,Contradicted,Disputed,Unknown}, explicitly experimental, not frozen. Formalizes KnownUnknown = Unknown + KnownMissingEvidence (e.g. 'we don't know whether the firewall permits the connection' AND we know the missing evidence is a FirewallTest), argued to be far more useful than a bare 'unknown' -- it becomes actionable via Unknown(C) + EvidenceRequired(C)=E => NextAction=Collect(E), with the information-theoretic framing X* = argmax_X E[H(Theta)-H(Theta|X)] as a design principle (not literally implemented everywhere): 'a good knowledge system should know what evidence would be most useful next.'

notations: Conflict is first an epistemic fact, not an error

sources.note: Step 181's founding principle: when two apparently-valid claims genuinely conflict, the system first records ConflictDetected(C1,C2) rather than declaring either side Wrong -- 'conflict is first an epistemic fact, not an error', the existence of disagreement being itself knowledge about the knowledge state. Rejects two naive resolution rules: 'latest wins' (Timestamp does not imply Truth -- a newer claim from a stale document can be weaker than an older claim from a production test) and 'highest confidence wins' (confidence numbers without semantics -- comparability, calibration, independence, subjectivity, cross-agent provenance -- create false precision; 'confidence alone does not resolve semantic conflict').

three load-bearing sites: frame-setting, authority chain into admission, the decision boundary (A6)

sources.note: Book chapter III.2's formal Definition-Knower: a distinguished agent (no symbol, no variation) owning the problem, purpose/goal G, IdealState, and final authority over commitment -- ratified as invariant I-1, graded READ via 'the three-regime chain' (measure-theory/Gita/step-series eras), the model's strongest single lineage finding since it is the only invariant that survived all three regimes unchanged. States ownership is load-bearing in exactly three places: (1) frame-setting -- G and IdealState change only by the Knower's act, no evidence accumulation or optimization pressure may adjust them, with the corpus recording a same-hour failure when this was violated; (2) the authority chain into admission -- the governed AcceptancePolicy chain (I-11) terminates at the Knower, closing an earlier 'unowned policy' hole by routing ownership through governance rather than a shortcut; (3) the decision boundary (A6, III.6) -- becoming bound to a proposition is the Knower's side of the line, in person or through governance structures. Clarifies ownership does not mean the Knower performs the epistemic labor (delegable to engines/selectors/auditors) but reserves exactly two non-delegable things: the standard ('what would satisfy me?') and the say-so (the binding act). States two negative clarifications: the Knower is not the system's user in a product sense, and not a component -- nothing implements the Knower, the architecture only records their acts and reserves decisions to them. Notes a graded-PARTIAL convergence with the separately-developed constitutional tradition protecting the same figure under the Ksetrajna lineage, with ownership of goal/standard established on the formal side only -- evidence of independent arrival, not identity.

rows.statement: 21.66-21.69: new evidence can invalidate premises/assumptions/rules/models/derivations/determinations within the cycle Evidence->Reasoning->Conclusion->Determination->Decision->Action->Observation->Revision, but proof objects are historical epistemic artifacts -- a previously valid proof can remain historically valid while its conclusion is no longer currently accepted (HistoricalValidity≠CurrentValidity); reasoning revision changes ProofStatus_t(pi)=Valid to Superseded or Invalidated at t+1 depending on contract, without deleting the old proof; minimal mutation prefers reconsidering only the dependency closure Affected(a) (LocalRevision over GlobalRecomputation), but this is not an unconditional law -- a global rule change may legitimately require broad recomputation, so minimality is itself contract- and dependency-dependent; rule and model governance must track identity/authority/version/provenance/effective-time/scope/approval-status/change-history (rules) and identity/version/training-lineage/validation-status/scope/limitations (models) -- a rule's mere existence in storage never makes it authorized.

sources.note: The proposed KR-ZOOM-02 set-anchored zoom design meant to repair KR-ZOOM-01's structural-counterfactual testing limitation.

rows.anchor: KR-ZOOM-02: Set-anchored Zoom. Instead of 'Zoom around ONE anchor dimension' ... 'Zoom around a SET of dimensions.' ... Question A ... B ... C ... D ... Now those questions can actually produce different answers.
rows.statement: Proposes the KR-ZOOM-02 design: instead of anchoring zoom to a single dimension (which structurally guarantees the host node cannot change), anchor to a SET of dimensions, illustrated with a business-database analogy (anchor set {Customer, Contract} instead of {Customer} alone), enabling four previously conflated questions to be asked and answered independently (did the observable result change; did structural relationships change; did another dimension become non-zero; did the business/epistemic determination change).
